Zesty food made by zesty and kind folk.,"Absolutely amazing tacos in this hole in the wall joint. Zesty food made by zesty and kind folk. Some of their food took me back to the yucatan peninsula. The comida takes time to get to the table but all in all, it's worth it. So many to-go orders being taken place and many tables scattered round the spot. Needless to say, the staff are big on courtesy and cleanliness. Their are about 6 fresh in house made salsa's to enjoy with the meal. The refreshing juices (aguas frescas) are made in house as well; with actual chunks of fruit and pulp. The juice is sweet and cold, pairing well with the savory food. I truly recommend the grande avocado quesadilla and the crispy tostada. Heck, the tacos are great as well. Their are many items on the menu, flexible and accommodating for any palette. Plenty of vegetarian items to choose from and the beans, tortillas are vegetarian (no lard). Bonus points! As many folk don't consume pork these days. Looking forward to revisiting and trying the nopal (cactus) and sopa (soup). Glad to have a warm spot such as Doña Lena in the neighborhood.",Sara I.,4/28/2021,5,,,,,,,,,America/Chicago,,,,,,Houston,,,,,,active,hidden,Draft
sara-review-verbena-coffee,Review,Sara's review of Verbena Coffee,Verbena Coffee,"Such a great little coffee shop in the neighborhood, and it hasn't even been opened for 2 years. They are thriving in the memorial area and it's wonderful to continue supporting local business.","Such a great little coffee shop in the neighborhood, and it hasn't even been opened for 2 years. They are thriving in the memorial area and it's wonderful to continue supporting local business. I love visiting independently owned coffee shops and trying various drinks they craft in house. My favorite here being the London fog latte. It is a special bevvie close to my heart and not everyone knows how to make it correctly. I dig the loose leaf earl grey tea blend which they steep in warmed foamy milk. They add a fragrant vanilla syrup to the bevvie (which is typically added to a London fog). They array of flavors and aroma made me happy. Bergamot flavour is sharp and on point. Sipping on this gray colored latte on a gray & rainy day brought forth a cosy appeal. Coffee drinks are nice as well; such as the brown sugar latte. The brown sugar syrup is also made in house. Surprisingly the drink is not that sweet which is great. Asking to add cinnamon to the drink really brings out the brown sugar flavour. Cappuccinos are solid as well. I look forward to revisiting and trying the sliced loaf cakes and croissants that are delivered from a local bakery. The interior is all woodsy with tan colored furniture. It reminds me of Scandinavia. Sometimes they have popups with various cafe businesses, such as Koffeteria. Always fun to see what goes on with the neighborhood cafe. review-rev-0208-59-diner,Review,Review: 59 Diner — 2010-05-19,59 Diner,"59 DINER! Whats the name behind it? Then... she told me that i`ve got it all wrong, and that it has to deal with the road highway 59! Hahah. The debat","59 DINER!
Whats the name behind it?
I told my sister its obviously due to the fact that diners were very popular in the fifties. Therefore, I suggested it was named after the year 1959.
Then... she told me that i`ve got it all wrong, and that it has to deal with the road highway 59! Hahah.
The debate still continues..
..Anyways.
My friends, sister, and I came here late at night, after enjoying ourselves at a concert. Right when we stepped in, I felt as if I had been transported to the 'happy days' years. We were seated promptly, and had courteous service. I was craving something cheesy, so I choose the grilled cheese sandwich. I hadn't had a gourmet cheese sandwich in forever, so it was nice to eat this up! The french fries that came a long were thin and crispy -- highly addictive.
My friends ordered the famous malts.They happily chugged down their malts, with an aftermath of a brain freeze!
59 Diner has a large menu chock full of items you don't usually find at other spots. It`s a nice change from the usual Denny`s and Ihops that are found nestled all around the 'burbs. review-rev-0181-bijan-persian-grill-sharpstown,Review,Review: Bijan Persian Grill — Sharpstown — 2010-05-19,Bijan Persian Grill — Sharpstown,"Kebabs and Rice! As simple and yet so flavourful as it can get. That is all I need when I come to Bijan Persian Grill. The location is right on Hilcroft, towards the entrance. You can`t miss it. The balcony juts out, and the place is quite big. Once you enter, immediately the staff seats you promptl","Kebabs and Rice!
As simple and yet so flavourful as it can get.
That is all I need when I come to Bijan Persian Grill.
The location is right on Hilcroft, towards the entrance. You can`t miss it. The balcony juts out, and the place is quite big.
Once you enter, immediately the staff seats you promptly. This has to be some of the best service I have received at a Persian restaurant. The waiters are calm and assuring, as well as helpful when deciding on the menu.
I have enjoyed the Koobideh as well as the Chicken Kebabs. The stews are delicious and slow cooked as well. The meat is perfectly cooked and juicy. One thing I love about Persian (Irani) food is that it does not need an overwhelming amount of spices and flavourings. It is just simple and so darn good.
The food is served with a platter of fresh herbs and feta cheese. The bread is rustic, crispy, and always warm. Tear a piece of bread, and wrap it around some herbs and cheese. Its like having pizza without the sauce.
On the table is this ""mystery spice"" everyone is unsure of. I will tell you right now what it is! The spice is actually a dried berry called Sumac. Dash it on top of your rice for a tart and pleasant surprise.
The saffron ice cream is exotic and rich. Its a change from regular flavoured ice cream. Do try it!
End the night with some sweet and relaxing Persian tea. It is aromatic, cardamom flavoured Earl Grey. Ah, splendid..",,5/19/2010,5,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,Houston,,,,,,hidden,hidden,Draft

review-rev-0214-bombay-pizza-express,Review,Review: Bombay Pizza Express — 2012-09-12,Bombay Pizza Express,"So ive known about Bombay Pizza Company from the very beginning, when they opened their original location in downtown Houston. I remember even having stepped inside their main location and having browsed throughout their menu. At the time I wasn't hungry, but I knew that I wanted to try the place out in the near future. That never happened due to the distance and proximity of the location..
Fast forward two years later, and they opened up a second location in Sugar Land. I finally got to try this place out last week and absolutely loved it. In fact, I ate there twice last week and tried out different foods during my stay. I wont go much into detail, but all I can say is that these folks mastered the art of fusion cuisine very well. I have enjoyed the pizzas, kati rolls, and their veggie burger. The spices and flavours infused within the food were just right. I made the right decision of having ordered the sweet potato fries with my veggie burger. The fries had a subtle hint of spice which went well with the natural taste of the sweet potato. A spicy ketchup relish was served along with these fries which I enjoyed. I'm not much of a french fry person, but these were darn good! The veggie burger was bursting with spices and flavor. It was quite strong actually, and I do believe that horseradish must have been mixed in that burger.
I like how their is a wide selection of items to choose from the menu, but there isnt too much going on, which is a good thing. The pizzas are nice and crispy, and the kati rolls are huge and filling. I ordered the tandoori paneer roll, as well as the tandoori shrimp roll, and enjoyed both. The naan wrapped around these rolls were fresh and crispy. A small side of chutney is served with these rolls which give them extra flavour.
Overall, I enjoyed my stay in this casual pizza restaurant. The place was crowded with families coming in and out. This place is fairly new, so its ul","I absolutely love banh mi sandwiches! It's great to finally have a banh mi restaurant not too far from Sugar Land. You dont have to drive all the way to the city, or get lost in Midtown! (Not that I dont love the city, but sometimes I get lazy to drive out there). This place is fairly new, so its ultra clean and shiny inside. The interior of the restaurant is spacious with many areas to sit.
I ordered the vegetarian tofu banh mi, that came with all the fix-ins. The tofu pieces were fried and crispy. I'm not a fan of fried food, but didnt mind it too much in my sandwich. The tofu was plain and bare-naked. Most places I go to, they spike the tofu with spices or lemongrass. I didnt mind it much that the tofu was plain, I simply dashed a bit of hot sauce and soy sauce in my sandwich. I did notice that the essential mayonnaise was missing from my meal. That is what binds a Vietnamese style sandwich! I'll make sure that they put it into my meal next time. I even asked the waiter if the mayo they serve is vegetarian, and he told me that it is. So i'm not sure why they forgot to add it, but it's all good. I also tried the soft rolls with shrimp. The rolls were fresh and soft and came with a hoisin style dipping sauce.
I also loved the fact that I was greeted kindly by the owner. He checked up on me often. The family that owns this cafe are courteous and caring. I'll be back soon enough to get my crispy sandwich fix!",,6/11/2013,4,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,Stafford,,,,,,hidden,hidden,Draft

I must say, Droubi`s makes the best darn Chicken Shawerma`s! I`m not saying that 'just cause. It must be that I`ve had good experience eating it more than two or three times. The Shawerma is layered with juicy succulent chicken. The yogurt sauce is tangy and garlicky. If you are not into tangy food, then don`t bother with complaining about the food. Most Mediterranean style yogurt is almost always on the sour/tangy side. A long with that factor, the sandwich is stuffed with thin slivers of pickles! How`s that for more sourness? I don`t mind it though, because I love pickles and anything tart. If you are not into that, then just ask for it to be removed.
The other foods that Droubi`s has to offer are good as well. I have enjoyed the Grape Leaves and the Kibbe. A long with that, the dessert`s are also nice. Try the Mamoul. Its basically like a fig newton. But instead its the real deal pastry! Big cookie, buttery, and stuffed with fruit.
The Market section of this place is huge. I always find it wonderful to eat, and then shop for the ingredients of what I just happened to eat! Makes it easier to remember what I had eaten on mind. There are a variety of fresh baked breads just been wrapped, as well as fresh cheeses, olive oils, and spices to purchase. It`s great to be able to find a variety of items.

You have the option to choose between biryani or burgers. I'm not much of a burger person so I ordered the 'whol,"I don't see the hype.
I happened to be in the area so I dropped by and ordered two chicken biryani's to-go. The menu selection that's offered here is quite minimal. Not that many choices. You have the option to choose between biryani or burgers. I'm not much of a burger person so I ordered the 'whole chicken bone-in biryani'. The vegetarian biryani didnt seem appealing and I love vegetarian food. Chicken seemed to be the right choice. But I was wrong.
So let me just say that I have high standards in judging any kind of biryani. I have great access to some of the best biryani through my aunty and mother. So its an item that I normally don't order at restaurants. Fanoosh so to speak specializes in biryani.. but it was a complete let down. The chicken biryani was bitter, dark and the chicken was completely dry. I had a tough time cutting through the poor dry chicken. Biryani is a speciality item within Pakistani/Indian cuisine that is known for its fragrance, color and flavor. The biryani here was lacking any of these qualities. It didn't hit the mark and tasted like a simple chicken curry that was baked with rice. I don't even know if the cooks behind the counter are aware of this. The flavor was under salted and it wasnt spicy. I'm not sure what a few of the reviewers mentioned in terms of spicy food. It was probably their first time trying biryani. What can they say? The raita was strangely sweet. When is raita ever sweet? Granted, i've tried tangy raita through the addition of buttermilk. But this raita only made the basic meal worse.

We had no plans on having dinner out.. but got hungry after having a nice chat at the nearby cafe. Came here upon convenience and it was quiet and empty inside. review-rev-0221-jus-mac-sugar-land,Review,Review: Jus’ Mac Sugar Land — 2012-06-13,Jus’ Mac Sugar Land,"I finally had the chance to try Jus' Mac a few days ago. I have known about this mac and cheese eatery since the original location was developed in the Heights. Fast forward two years, and I am sitting in a location that is tucked away in my neighborhood. It's good to know that this eatery has expan","I finally had the chance to try Jus' Mac a few days ago. I have known about this mac and cheese eatery since the original location was developed in the Heights. Fast forward two years, and I am sitting in a location that is tucked away in my neighborhood. It's good to know that this eatery has expanded and is now in close proximity to me. My friend and I randomly went the other day, and had a nice experience. The interior of the restaurant is cute and casual with an urban feel. I like the simplicity of the restaurant, and how it showcases various concoctions of macaroni and cheese. There are even panini's featured on the menu, which is wonderful, as not everyone is a fan of mac and cheese.
So I tried the popeye mac and cheese, which consisted of a creamy white cheese, tossed with baby spinach, mushrooms, and onions. The order arrived as soon as possible, and the mac and cheese was crisp and golden to perfection. The dish was served in a small cast iron skillet, and the meal was hot and bubbly. As a huge fan of mac and cheese, I happily finished my meal without any guilt. The flavours were perfectly seasoned, and well balanced. I appreciated the fact that my dish was not too salty, as most other restaurants serve a rather salty mac and cheese.
Overall I had a good experience at Jus Mac, and will be back soon again. Its nice to have a unique restaurant in town that showcases an American classic. This place defines that sort of image, and will definitely do well during the fall season, when people are looking for warm food that's nourishing and comforting!",,6/13/2012,4,https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xiWWq_aFR5i-BNVRy8Lykn_TofkGpm4_/view?usp=drivesdk,,,Needs review,,,,,,,,,,,Sugar Land,,,,,,active,hidden,Draft

Upon entering around lunch time.. the restaurant was bustling with people dining in. I couldn't decide what I wanted to order, so I went ahead with the chicken shawarma. My sister ordered the chicken kebab wrap with paratha bread. It took quite some time for our meal to arrive to our table. My chicken shawarma was seasoned with Indo-Pak seasonings. The tahini sauce inside the wrap was thin and watery. Most of it leaked out of the other end of my wrap as I ate it. The french fries that came with my meal were cold. I dont eat french fries that often, so I barely ate them. I was looking forward to a Levantine style Chicken Shawarma.. but that is not what I got. I should have realized this in the beginning, due to the restaurant being of South Asian influence. Other than that.. my meal was still decent. It was healthier than the other options and not spicy. I ordered Pakistani style chai to end my meal.. and it was good. The steaming cup of chai was made with fresh milk. It was simple and not spiked with spices as Indian chai usually is.
If I ever have a chance to come around this spot again, i'll definitely try the hardcore Pakistani dishes such as the Chicken Karahi or the Nihari.

It is flavourful and not too spicy. Every dish has its own unique appeal to it. The family that owns this restaurant are very friendly and welcoming.
The only downside is that there are no descriptions or pictures on the menu. So it makes it a bit difficult on choosing what to order. I was in the mood for a burrito, it had been several months since I had dropped by here. .
I`m SO glad that I opted for a burrito rather than a bowl!
The fact that Mission Burrito has a variety of selection keeps this place first in mind when I am craving a burrito.
There are several different tortillas you can select from: flour, wheat, tomato, or spinach.
I chose the spinach tortilla with cilantro rice, shrimp, beans, vegetables, sour cream, and guacamole.
I love how their are several different salsas to pick from. I usually pick two salsas which ends up giving my burrito a spicy and zesty kick. I also had corn in my burrito which gave a mellow sweet taste mixed in with the spicy savoury-ness. It paired so well! The grilled shrimp were delicious! Fresh, plump, and perfectly seasoned. I also decided on the guacamole (extra charge) which was flavourful and savoury. My burrito was huge but quite satisfying!
They also have these mega-sized chocolate chip cookies in front of the cashier counter. I think I have my eye on them & will definitely try them next time. Cant go wrong with a huge cookie. .

Naha Thai is fantastic.. ! From the food, to the environment, as well as the service.. there isn't much to say except that it's warm and cozy.
The owners are quite friendly and talkative; it makes all the difference in the world with a chatty diner such as myself. I enjoy relishing in conversations, especially with older folk that are full of wisdom. The folks that run this place are talkative and quite accommodating. The food is tasty and packs in a punch of heat. I love the fact that they use fresh red chilies in most of their items, instead of just ground red pepper. The pad thai here is light, fresh and crisp. Far from the typical greasy bowl types. It was nice to eat a different variation of it.. typically Northern Thai style. Every region has its own take.. but this one was refreshing. The penang curry is great here as well. Aromatic and bubbling. The coconut milk is creamy and brimming with different veggies. I ordered the vegetarian option and found it to be delightful. Will definitely try a meat item next time and pair it with a different curry. I'm picky with curries but I can honestly say this one was the better one that I've had. Looking forward to revisiting and trying their soups, tea + so much more. The echoes of the old restaurant that used to be here are gone. This new spot is better. I'm glad Naha is in this part of town. We needed to crank up the heat in sweet old sugar land.",,7/26/2022,4,https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Ynii8goM2Q9e2gRwtdp0F3LCMRlVOurn/view?usp=drivesdk,,,Needs review,https://drive.google.com/file/d/1qleBXJDDkP7PhuU7GH7fNxySBgAeD9Rp/view?usp=drivesdk,,,,,,,,,,Sugar Land,,,,,,active,hidden,Draft

review-rev-0245-nazifs,Review,Review: Nazif’s — 2013-04-06,Nazif’s,"Having been to Turkiye recently, and having been influenced with many Turkish friends.. My family and I were greeted kindly, and were given p","Having been to Turkiye recently, and having been influenced with many Turkish friends.. I would have to say Nazif's restaurant cooks up some pretty authentic food. I recently came here on a weekend afternoon and to my surprise it wasn't too busy. My family and I were greeted kindly, and were given prompt service. Our food came on time and all of our meals were delicious.
We ordered the kibbi (icli kofte) and it was nice, crunchy, and spicy. The lamacun (flat-bread with meat) was flavourful and vibrant when mixed with the pickled cabbage. The kimali pide (meat pie) was hearty with meat and studded with nuts and parsley on top. For dessert, we ordered the rice pudding, and it was cold, thick, and creamy. We ended our meal with some Turkish style tea. This sort of cuisine cant be ended without any tea. There lunch prices are a bit steep, but it's still a good deal when considering all you get. I can honestly say that all the dishes were made well and were quite filling. I'll probably even bring my picky Turkish friends sometime soon. I'm looking forward in trying out their other dishes as well. There are some specific dishes here that I haven't spotted in the other Turkish restaurants that are in town. review-rev-0118-pangea-bar-grill,Review,Review: Pangea Bar & Grill — 2018-01-23,Pangea Bar & Grill,I recently visited Pangea with my sister and a good friend of ours. We came here on the night of New Years Eve. The outside of the restaurant was vividly glowing at night. The inside was lit up as well. It was spacious and very decorative. I like the style of this place. Makes me feel like i'm sitti,"I recently visited Pangea with my sister and a good friend of ours. We came here on the night of New Years Eve. The outside of the restaurant was vividly glowing at night. The inside was lit up as well. It was spacious and very decorative. I like the style of this place. Makes me feel like i'm sitting inside a Sultan's palace. The inside of Pangea is huge. Plenty of indoor seating as well as outdoor seating which is towards the back. The outdoor seating is ideal for those who are into hookah. I'm not fond of that stuff, so i'm glad the inside of the place wasn't reeking of hookah stench. Pangea is not like the dingy hookah cafes we have in Houston which are overcrowded and obnoxious. Its an actual family style restaurant with a good feel to it. We sat ourselves upon a comfortable couch towards the front with a large coffee table. Throughout the night we received warm and attentive service. The manager and waiters were very friendly and made us feel welcomed.
In terms of the food: I recommend trying the Pangea sampler: it consists of 4 of each item: grape leaves, falafel, kibbe, and empanadas. The food was freshly prepared as it took some time and it came out hot and crisp. Absolutely enjoyed each item off the sampler and paired quite well with their cardamom tea. The tea consists of fragrant black tea gently simmered with cardamom and served in a large tea pot. The fried food was drenched down with a hot cup of tea. Empanada's were made from puff pastry, instead of the typical flour dough. Two of the empanadas came with cheese and the other two with beef. Grape leaves were tart and tender. Falafel was crisp and green inside. Fluffy pita bread was served in addition to the sampler. I'd like to try more items off the menu next time around, such as the koshary and hummus. You'll find Egyptian, Levantine, and South American cuisine on the menu. A bit of something for everyone. We were treated to baklava on the house that night. Baklava was a bit on the dry side but still had a nice and sweet taste. The gesture was appreciated. This place is family friendly and the crowd doubled in size later in the night. A belly dancer showed up and was fiercely dancing to the loud music. It was a good night. I can see myself revisiting for lunch or dinner. It's a cool spot to hangout with family or friends. Checkout Pangea Cafe & Grill if you're interested in Mediterranean cuisine with a touch of true hospitality.",,1/23/2018,4,https://drive.google.com/file/d/1U7EdiN2mZDPr8d82fNU8l43Vo-mTbSpP/view?usp=drivesdk,,,Needs review,"https://drive.google.com/file/d/1POaWyu9UWONUXl_60CHKm-XPuoWJviPy/view?usp=drivesdk

Being as I am, very much into cooking, I feel as if this is the one stop shop place for my foodie menu. I can find all sorts of unique items in the produce, dry goods, and meats section.
As soon as you enter, take a left. Once you`ve done that look above you! There`s a marvelous conveyor belt churning up puffy, fresh, pita breads. Pick up any of the packages of breads, and you will notice the steam against the bag, and how the bread just feels in your hands. Freshness at its finest!
Whenever I drop by to Phoenicia, I take quite some time venturing around the very tall aisles filled with items. It`s even more wonderful that this market has a section with a cafe and bakery. There`s nothing like chowing down on a roasted chicken wrap with garlic sauce, and moving a long with your cart at the same time. Hehe. Multi tasking at its finest. ;) They have an area filled with tables where you can sit down as well. The dessert items in the bakery are just eye pleasing, as well as delicious. Try the Kanafeh, which is a sweet cheese dessert, topped with semolina (halva) layered on top. The Baklava`s are great here as well. Tom Kha Gai Soup is a bit sour,"Thai Siam is a cozy and small restaurant.
The decoration inside is of a traditional and cultural feel. I love places that give off that vibe.
I have enjoyed the Pad Kee Mao and Pad Thai. Both dishes are served with thin rice noodles and flavourful meats and vegetables.
Tom Kha Gai Soup is a bit sour to my taste. I know that lemon grass and lime juice are used, but it was a bit too over powering. The soup is served in an interesting bowl that makes it hard to take out the contents. I do like how they thought of using a traditional soup bowl, but it is not practical.
For appetizer's, I recommend Sate and Tod Mun Pla (fish cakes). The Sate is served with a beautiful peanut sauce which is highly addictive. (I LOVE peanut butter!) The Tod Mun Pla is basically spicy fried minced fish cakes. It is served with a spicy red pepper cucumber relish. Delicious!
The curries here are warm, fragrant, and fill up your bellie! I have been pleased with both the Green Curry, and Massamun Curry. They are rich and spicy, served up with a side of steaming jasmine rice.
For a refreshing drink, sip on some Thai Iced Tea. Although I would not recommend ordering it with tapioca. The pearls are overly cooked. My drink was tasty, minus the pearls which were too soft.
Overall, I always enjoy my experience at this quiet neighborhood restaurant. The waitresses are kind and graceful as well. Also, they always have Food Network playing on their television! Yay, my favourite channel. ;)",,5/28/2010,4,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,Sugar Land,,,,,,hidden,hidden,Draft

review-rev-0063-the-oceanaire-seafood-room,Review,Review: The Oceanaire Seafood Room — 2023-09-12,The Oceanaire Seafood Room,"3 stars experience during Houston Restaurant Weeks. Boy, were we all excited to dine in at this restaurant. It is a Houston classic! From the submarine looking terrain, to the large windows at the corner facing one of the busiest streets in Houston. It's the Galleria after all, and its one of the mo","3 stars experience during Houston Restaurant Weeks.
Boy, were we all excited to dine in at this restaurant. It is a Houston classic!
From the submarine looking terrain, to the large windows at the corner facing one of the busiest streets in Houston. It's the Galleria after all, and its one of the most popular spots to visit. This restaurant has been around for over 20 years, and for some of us, it was our very first time.
I do believe they could have had better choices in regards to their food menu with HRW. This is all in regards to food allergies, mind you. So thats something we take seriously. But we came on a mission! To dine in on HRW style menu which benefits the local Houston Food banks.
Their regular menu looks great and appealing. We may revisit and try items from their everyday menu. We did try their sushi and we loved it. The sushi was fresh and flavorful. It retained its shape well and came with a burst of flavor. My second favorite was the smoked salmon. It was chunky, held its shape and it had a great umami yet mellow flavor as well. Paired well with the bold marinated onions, capers, relish and crispy crackers.
I did like the shrimp fried rice, it was flavorful and well seasoned - however it was quite luke-warm by the time it reached our table. Reason being? They forgot to deliver our order to the table. We waited for ages after being served appetizers. So much time passed by that I had to flag down a waiter from far away, just to get his notice and ask him what happened to our food?
He quickly went in, back of the house and grabbed our meals. So basically our meals were sitting BOH, chillin and getting cold. No apologies or ""I'm sorry for the delay in your food"". Instead he mentioned, ""Oh, we're packed and having a busy day here"". Definitely didn't seem like it, with most of the room being empty. Just one day before, my entire office dined in here for HRW. What must have happened then? Not enough employees to accommodate diners needs. Lack of customer service was the down fall of our experience dining here at the Oceanaire.
Dessert was good. It was ordered from their regular menu as its not provided with HRW. We opted for the key lime pie and it was definitely one of the better ones we've all had. Super tart, sweet and refreshing. Perfect on the palate after consuming mellow oceanic foods.
Again, we all enjoyed our food. Totally look forward to revisiting and trying items from their regular menu. This is a nice spot to bring out of town guests. They have many non-seafood items as well for those that aren't much into seafood. We're just hoping for warmer and keen attentive service next time around for such a posh and elaborate spot such as this.
Until next time!",,9/12/2023,3,https://drive.google.com/file/d/1yWvZtZ1cnSA3T1qWk8nvryzn0m7Pp3LW/view?usp=drivesdk,,,Needs review,"https://drive.google.com/file/d/1R4uyDzZYaO4BRK6UAC1b3xqm5XKYSnAt/view?usp=drivesdk

I have only came in here on a few visits to pick up sweets. Almond croissant","""Aw, what a cute little patisserie!""
Those were the words that came out of my mouth as I found this little gem, tucked in Uptown Park. It was also my first visit to the park. Small, pretty, with little shops here and there.
I have only came in here on a few visits to pick up sweets. Almond croissant is the first word muttered out of my mouth, as I explain to the cashier on what to fill my bag with. Then comes scones, brownie, and cranberry bar.
The almond croissant is generously loaded with almonds, and marzipan. It is huge, and can feed up to three people. Thats if you don`t mind sharing! ;)
The Swiss brownies have the perfect amount of semi sweet cocoa, and have a chewy moist taste. They are definitely the gourmet fix for brownies!
Scones are heavy, and crumble in your mouth. Just the way they should be. It is dotted with crispy cinnamon sugar.
Cranberry bars are refreshingly zesty! A nice blend of sweetness with just the right amount of tartness. The lemon gives it a clean taste.
Oh yes... also petit fours! How can I forget to mention them. They are mini little cakes that are wrapped around a green coloured marzipan layer. The inside of the cake is layered with a soft filling of raspberry. Quite wonderful!

review-rev-0014-tnsberg-brygge,Review,Review: Tønsberg Brygge — 2022-02-10,Tønsberg Brygge,"Tønsberg is quite a beautiful little town. Historical and considered to be the oldest town in Norway. In fact, Tonsberg Old Cemetery contains 22 war graves, of the First World War, 14 of them unidentified by name, b","Tønsberg is quite a beautiful little town. Historical and considered to be the oldest town in Norway. It became an important trading center and was founded by Vikings in the 9th century. In fact, Tonsberg Old Cemetery contains 22 war graves, of the First World War, 14 of them unidentified by name, but all naval casualties from the Battle of Jutland in 1916. This town is charming with it's cobblestone streets, in particular near their shopping district. I used to live in this town back in 2017, for about half of the year. Visiting the brygge, (pier) was always such a nice and tranquil escape. Their are plenty of restaurants outlined near the brygge. Some of the restaurants were diverse within their culinary range and the food wasn't too bad. I did not have the best culinary experience in Norway, but they did have a decent Indian restaurant by the pier. Local caught seafood was fresh and of good quality. They typically displayed that sort of fare during the farmers market. The pier would be freezing towards the autumn and winter seasons. The townsfolk launch their old historical boats during the holiday season and it is a sight to see. Many of the cafes, coffee shops and restaurants would close by 8-9 pm. Grocery stores and many shoppes were closed on Sundays. As an American, it was a bit of a culture shock. But the major differences I experienced in this town drove me towards introspection and deep growth. The glassy icey water reminded of a mirror upon self reflection. I may have been on the outside looking in, but it was a beautiful ponderous ride. I recommend visiting the pier and just overall experiencing this quiet, elegant town.",,2/10/2022,4,https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Nlqgfob65ohDQk_Q42T0WPHp1Pv_myrD/view?usp=drivesdk,,,Needs review,"https://drive.google.com/file/d/1qhB92W3EGYUBVmVhSNMSQhCdi_hfZooR/view?usp=drivesdk

I still made my way here as the cravings for baklava were unreal. When I stepped inside, no one asked if I n","A shabby and rundown strip on Richmond Ave.. Zeyad Bakery & Sweets offers up some savory and sweet Palestinian baked goods.
The outside of the bakery gives off an unkempt and uninviting feel. I still made my way here as the cravings for baklava were unreal. When I stepped inside, no one asked if I needed any help. I'd say this bakery is a good place to order a large quantity of desserts for a party. I'd like to try the Levantine pizza on my next trip. It's called Sfina and its layered with ground beef and tomatoes. They have one with ground thyme (zaatar) and cheese as well (manakeesh). Cedar Bakery is right near this plaza.. so the competition is stiff up on the bakers.
